findings.title: One outage is reported in four places, and the header brand slot becomes a status line
findings.evidence:
shell-loading__en-desktop-dark.png: 'Waiting for connection…' appears as the bold header brand (top-left of the content area), in the sidebar 'Current warehouse' slot, and as the card status line, next to the 'Can't reach the server' banner. The Thai captures repeat 'กำลังรอการเชื่อมต่อ…' the same way. Source: DesktopShell.tsx:207-212 renders `name ?? t("waitingForConnection")` in the semibold header brand

. DesktopShell.loading.test.tsx:205-212 asserts the same text in the sidebar warehouse slot and in the header.
findings.fix: Make the banner the only place that explains the outage. Leave the header brand empty or keep its aria-hidden Skeleton while the connection stalls, show the sidebar warehouse line as a Skeleton, and keep the card's skeleton with either no label or a neutral 'กำลังโหลดสินค้าสำเร็จรูป…' instead of repeating the connection message.

notes: All 12 images were read as pixels. Shell is clean and consistent across th/en and light/dark: header carries the organisation name (D3), sidebar/drawer carry โยงกิจ/Yongkit, search triggers state their scope ('ค้นหาเมนูหรือพนักงาน… / Pages or employees…') with a ⌘K hint only on pointer devices, accessible names are complete (e.g. 'เปลี่ยนภาษาเป็น English', theme toggle with aria-pressed, drawer as named dialog), axe clean, no overflow. Cross-screen: (1) the Finished goods search placeholder is hard-clipped at 390 px in both locales (filed on shell-page; owned by the FG toolbar, so the FG group may file it too). (2) Workspace context is shown three ways: phone header shows the warehouse code only, rail header shows code plus name, expanded desktop shows it only in the sidebar select; each is reasonable but the full warehouse name is never readable on phone or expanded desktop with the long seeded name. (3) The theme icon is accent-tinted in dark (moon) but muted in light (sun), a small emphasis mismatch. (4) Rail search vs active-tile ambiguity (filed on shell-rail). The search dialog itself is not in this image group, so the benchmark search anchors were not scored here.

All 12 images were read as pixels. Both screens share a solid base: full-height sheet on phone and a 672 px dialog on desktop, 48 px rows on phone, a visible active-row bar plus tint (not colour alone), match highlighting in titles and codes (Linear pattern), alias explanation 'ตรงกับ “employees”' for Latin queries on Thai titles, a 'Scroll for more results' cue, and an Esc hint that switches from ปิด/close to ล้าง/clear once text is typed. Dark-mode muted text on the selected row (oklch 0.72 on oklch 0.32) works out to about 5:1, so I found no contrast failure; axe is clean on every capture. The recurring cross-screen issue is a type-size inversion: descriptive text (group description and AI row detail/privacy at text-sm) is larger than the group headings and record meta at text-xs (SearchDialog.tsx:660/672/915/923/968). It shows most on the typed AI row, so it is filed on search-results, and once on search-empty for the examples block. Coverage items are filed as P3 so they do not act as defects under D9. Minor parity note, not filed: the Latin query 'EMP' returns two tasks in English but one in Thai, because the Thai task titles have no matching alias; the product owner may want aliases kept in step across locales. Items covered by D12–D16 (no bottom bar, no warehouse code lookup, AI as a list row, no scope chips, the disclosure copy itself) were not scored down.

I read all 12 images as pixels, along with the a11y snapshots for search-ai-running th-mobile, search-no-match th-desktop and shell-loading en-mobile. Search dialog: no-match and AI-running follow D14 and D16 closely. The AI row is labelled, reuses the query and comes first when nothing matches. It becomes a pending row with a status role and a Cancel button. The 'Go to' shortcuts are ordered with Warehouse first on the Finished goods page (D15). Phone rows and Cancel are 48 CSS px tall, and both themes look legible. The dialog title changes from 'ค้นหา' to 'ค้นหาด้วย AI' while AI runs, which is consistent across locales. Not captured in this group, and so not scored: the settled AI answer and whether it shows the pages it used (Notion pattern), the AI error/cancelled state, and the shell-loading drawer on the phone. Shell loading: the banner gives the reason and the next step ('The app keeps retrying automatically', Reload page) and keeps the layout. The cross-screen issue is that the shell repeats the connection status in the header brand and the sidebar warehouse slot rather than leaving them as placeholders; the findings are filed on shell-loading. Minor: the English sidebar line 'The menu appears once the server connects' has no full stop. The shell-loading banner is a role=status region that also contains the Reload button, so assistive tech announces the button label along with the message.

I read all 10 images as pixels. The not-found page renders outside the signed-in shell (product wordmark, language and theme only). The route error renders inside the shell with breadcrumb, Back, h1, a danger Notice, Retry plus a named recovery destination, and a copyable reference with module and time. The two screens use the same PageHeader type scale and the same button heights (48 px on phone, 36 px dense on desktop), and their copy matches in tone across th and en. Thai dates use the Buddhist era (5 พ.ย. 2569 21:27) and English uses "Nov 5, 2026, 9:28 PM". I saw no clipped Thai tone marks in the headings, the alert title or the buttons. The retrying capture (#10) keeps both buttons in place, and the copied capture (#9) changes the icon to a check and the label to คัดลอกแล้ว. The phone header truncates the organisation name more in Thai than in English because the "English" switch label is wider; that is a shell-wide issue covered by other groups and involves seeded names (D8), so I did not file it here. Both screens capture each locale in only one theme.
